A Run Target request will record the "pending Run Target".
The cyclic main loop will check in each iteration for a recorded pending Run Target
and initiates the Run Target transition when in kSuccess or kUndefinedState state.
In kComponentRecovery the ongoing component RAs are stopped first and the graph
kUndefinedState is not terminal. Every main loop iteration leaves it, towards a
recorded pending Run Target request if there is one and towards the fallback Run
Before a new transition can be started any currently ongoing jobs need to finish.
kAborting is the state that is waiting for jobs to finish. No new jobs will be started
in this state. When the in-flight job count reaches zero (no more jobs in process),
Requests made while in kAborting do not change the state immediately, but only change the
target for the transition that will be started in kUndefinedState.
kComponentRecovery is entered when a component of the active Run Target terminates
unexpectedly and has a component recovery action (RA) configured (e.g. restart).
Component RAs are only executed in kSuccess and kComponentRecovery. A failure during a
Run Target transition always aborts the transition, even if a component RA is configured.
Only the failed component is recovered, its dependents keep running. The active
Run Target is still reported as active while in this state, and a request for the
active Run Target does not interrupt the recovery. Further failures with a component
RA are recovered in parallel. When the last component RA succeeds, the graph returns
to kSuccess. If a component RA fails, or a component without a component RA fails,
the remaining component RAs are stopped and the graph leaves via kAborting or
kUndefinedState towards the pending Run Target, or the fallback Run Target otherwise.
If a component RA cannot be queued for execution (only during shutdown, when the worker
queue is stopped), the graph aborts as for a failed component RA.
A supervision failure does not change the graph state. The process is killed (SIGKILL)
and the resulting unexpected termination drives the reaction described above.
